title.raw: 卷一百三十七 列傳第六十二 郭子儀子:曜 子:晞 晞孫:承嘏 子:曖 曖子:釗 鏦 銛 曖孫:曙 母弟:幼明 幼明子:昕 Volume 137 Biographies 62: Guo Ziyi and Son: Yao, Son: Xi, Xi's Grandson: Cheng Gu, Son: Ai, Zi's Sons: Zhao, Cong, Xian, Ai's Grandson: Shu, Uncle: You Ming, You Ming's Son: Xin

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 郭子儀子:曜 子:晞 晞孫:承嘏 子:曖 曖子:釗 鏦 銛 曖孫:曙 母弟幼:明 幼明子:昕
value.en: Guo Ziyi's sons included Yao and Xi; Xi's grandson was Chenggu. He also had a son named Ai, whose sons were Zhao, Cong, and Xian, and whose grandson was Shu. His younger brother by the same mother was Youming, and Youming's son was Xin.
value.literal: Guo Ziyi — sons: Yao; son: Xi; Xi's grandson: Chenggu; son: Ai; Ai's sons: Zhao, Cong, and Xian; Ai's grandson: Shu; uterine younger brother You: Ming; Youming's son: Xin.

value.zh: 曜，性沉靜，資貌瑰傑。
value.en: Yao was sedate by nature, with a splendid and commanding presence.
value.literal: Yao — nature sedate and quiet, endowment and appearance splendid and outstanding.

value.zh: 累從節度府辟署，破虜有功，為開陽府果毅都尉。
value.en: He was repeatedly recruited to military commissioner staffs, won merit defeating the enemy, and was made Guoyi Commander of Kaiyang District.
value.literal: Repeatedly recruited to military commissioner staffs; defeated barbarians with merit; made Guoyi Commander of Kaiyang District.

value.zh: 至德初，推子儀功，授衛尉卿，累進太子詹事、太原郡公。
value.en: At the beginning of the Zhide era (756), in recognition of Guo Ziyi's merit, he was appointed Guardian of the Imperial Insignia and was later promoted to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince's Household and Duke of Taiyuan.
value.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, in recognition of Ziyi's merit, he was appointed Guardian of the Imperial Insignia; promoted in succession to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince's Household and Duke of Taiyuan.

value.zh: 子儀專征伐，曜留治家事，少長無閑言。
value.en: While Guo Ziyi devoted himself to campaigns, Yao remained at home to manage the household — and among the family, young and old alike, there was no gossip.
value.literal: Ziyi devoted himself to campaigns; Yao remained to manage household affairs — among young and old, no idle talk.

value.zh: 諸弟或飾池館，盛車服，曜獨以朴簡自處。
value.en: Some of his brothers ornamented their pools and halls and went about in lavish carriages and robes. Yao alone lived plainly.
value.literal: Some of his brothers ornamented pools and halls, lavish in carriages and robes; Yao alone lived in plain simplicity.

value.zh: 子儀罷兵，遷太子少保，昆弟六人，共制拜官。
value.en: When Guo Ziyi laid down his arms, Yao was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince. The six brothers jointly regulated official appointments within the family.
value.literal: When Ziyi laid down arms, Yao was transferred to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; six brothers jointly regulated official appointments.

value.zh: 子儀薨，以遺命簿上四朝所賜名馬珍物，德宗復賜之，乃悉散諸弟。
value.en: When Guo Ziyi died, his will listed the famous horses and treasures granted by four reigns. Emperor Dezong re-granted them, and Yao distributed everything among his brothers.
value.literal: When Ziyi passed away, per his will the register listed famous horses and treasures granted by four reigns; Dezong re-granted them, and Yao distributed all to his brothers.

value.zh: 居喪以禮，疾甚，或勸茹蔥薤，終不屬口。
value.en: He observed mourning rites properly. When he grew very ill, some urged him to eat leeks and chives, but he never let them touch his lips.
value.literal: He observed mourning according to rites; very ill, some urged leeks and chives — he never let them touch his lips.

value.zh: 後盧杞秉政，忌勳族，子儀婿太僕卿趙縱、少府少監李洞清、光祿卿王宰皆以次得罪。
value.en: Later, when Lu Qi held power, he was jealous of meritorious clans. Guo Ziyi's sons-in-law — Grand Master of Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Assistant Director of the Palace Stores Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai — were punished one after another.
value.literal: Later Lu Qi held power, jealous of meritorious clans; Ziyi's sons-in-law — Grand Master of Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Assistant Director of the Palace Stores Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai — were punished in turn.

value.zh: 奸人幸其危，多論奪田宅奴婢，曜大恐，獨宰相張鎰力保護。
value.en: Villains preyed on the family's peril and seized many estates and slaves. Yao was greatly afraid, and only Chief Minister Zhang Huan forcefully protected him.
value.literal: Villains preyed on their peril and seized many estates and slaves; Yao was greatly afraid — only Chief Minister Zhang Huan forcefully protected him.

value.zh: 德宗稍聞之，詔有司曰：「尚父子儀有大勳力，保乂王家，嘗誓山河，琢金石，許宥十世。
value.en: When Emperor Dezong gradually learned of this, he issued an edict to the offices: "Imperial Father Guo Ziyi rendered great service and preserved the imperial house. An oath sworn on mountains and rivers and carved in metal and stone granted his line exemption for ten generations.
value.literal: Dezong gradually heard of it and issued an edict the offices, saying, "Imperial Father Ziyi had great merit, preserved and governed the royal house, once sworn on mountains and rivers, carved in metal and stone, granted exemption for ten generations.

value.zh: 前日其家市田宅奴婢，而無賴者以尚父歿，妄論奪之，自今有司毋得受。」
value.en: Recently his family purchased estates and slaves, yet rogues, citing Imperial Father's death, falsely seized them. From now on the offices shall not accept such claims."
value.literal: The other day his family purchased estates and slaves, yet rogues, citing the Imperial Father's death, falsely seized them — from now on the offices shall not accept such claims."

value.zh: 建中三年，卒，贈太子太傅，諡曰孝。
value.en: In the third year of the Jianzhong era (782) he died. He was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and granted the posthumous name Xiao.
value.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he died; posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; posthumous name Xiao.

value.zh: 初，曜襲代國公，食二千戶。
value.en: Initially Yao inherited the title Duke of Dai, with a fief of two thousand households.
value.literal: Initially Yao inherited the title Duke of Dai, with a fief of two thousand households.

value.zh: 貞元初，詔減半以封晞、曖、映、曙，人二百五十戶。
value.en: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era (785), an edict halved the fief to enfeoff Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu with two hundred fifty households each.
value.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, an edict halved the fief to enfeoff Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu — two hundred fifty households each.

value.zh: 未幾，復詔四人各減五十戶，封曜子鋒、晤子鐇各百戶雲。
value.en: Before long, another edict reduced each of the four by fifty households and enfeoffed Yao's son Feng and Wu's son Zheng with one hundred households each.
value.literal: Before long, another edict reduced each of the four by fifty households and enfeoffed Yao's son Feng and Wu's son Zheng with one hundred households each.

value.descriptorSuggestion: Son of Zhang Hua; companion to crown prince
